originality.rationale: Full-text comparison establishes distinct claims: the exact model source (Nowak et al. 2020) derives deterministic infinite-population phase portraits with a power-law mean-field panel approximation, not the finite joint equilibrium of without-replacement panels. Herrerías-Azcué and Galla (2019) give exact one-opinion marginals for LINEAR imitation, not two-neighbor unanimous nonlinear conformity. Peralta et al. (2018) treat only binary noisy-voter nonlinearities; Mobilia (2015) studies binary zealot dynamics. Standard detailed balance is not itself asserted to be new. The motivated all-size discrete modal reduction, no-reentrance and exact two discontinuous six-agent mode thresholds are not implications of these results. Relevant broad and specific semantic searches yielded no statement-equivalent result; historical priority remains a risk.
residual_risks: Some older statistical-mechanics multitype quadratic urn models could contain a strong general stationary-maxima implication not indexed under noisy voter terminology.
Source comparisons were conducted without independent subject-expert validation; no exhaustive bibliographic priority guarantee.
The standard micro-reversibility trick itself is not new; originality is assessed only for the full finite-mode theorem and exact N=6 modal staircase.

value.rationale: Genuine finite invariant-distribution modes are different observables from mean-field stationary concentrations or one-species marginals. The nontrivial all-size high-dimensional-to-one-leader mode reduction and no-reentrance monotonicity provide structurally useful new constraints. The natural minimal (N=6,s=3) example has exact radical two-jump modal thresholds and skips two intermediate leader sizes, a nontrivial finite-state ordering phenomenon. No downstream theorem or thermodynamic limit is claimed.
